title: Barred spiral bares all
caption: Barred spiral galaxy UGC 12158, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: UGC 12158 · constellation Pegasus · about 400 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The barred spiral UGC 12158 faces Hubble head-on here, its structure laid out in fine detail. Just to the lower left of the center is a bright blue star. Unlike the several foreground stars around it, this one is a supernova inside the galaxy itself, about 400 million light-years away.

UGC 12158 is a textbook example of a barred spiral in the Hubble sequence, a scheme that sorts galaxies by shape. Its arms sweep out from a bar-shaped center. About two thirds of spirals have bars, which are thought to funnel gas to the middle, where it piles up and forms new stars. Astronomers think bars slowly fade over time, so these galaxies eventually become regular spirals.

A galaxy's appearance barely changes over millions of years, but a supernova is brief. This one, SN 2004ef, was found in September 2004 by a pair of British amateur astronomers, and these Hubble data were part of the follow-up.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.33 x 2.00 arcminutes) and distance (400 million light years), the frame spans roughly 271,000 × 233,000 light-years. Its light set out about 400 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Blue light (F475W) is shown in blue, yellow light (F606W) in green, and red light (F814W) plus a filter isolating glowing hydrogen in red.
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, and the hydrogen filter picks out glowing gas that ordinary color vision would not isolate.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The exposures were 1160, 700, 700 and 1200 seconds, and the picture spans about 2.3 arcminutes.
alt: A face-on barred spiral galaxy with a bright blue point just to the lower left of its center, and several foreground stars.
